metadata.note: cli-explainer spine, weekly work report, claude-hai channel. Episode 10, from the last pushed commit on chore/recipe-lifecycle-frontmatter (6428457; origin contains it and the branch is in sync). FRAMEWORK: three questions for any count of problems — DOES IT CONTRADICT A CLAIM / WHICH LIST DID YOU MATCH AGAINST / DID THE GUARD EVER FIRE. Hero beat is B05, the survey that said 42 of 91 recipes had built scripts because it matched any mentioned scripts/ path including legacy scaffolds; narrowed to the six canonical steps it is zero. Falsifiability beat is B08: while fact-checking this episode my own grep returned 98 where the checker says 97, because it matched a .yaml file — the same error as the 42. 97/80/90/554 reproduced by running the checker read-only; the pure prepend verified independently from the diff structure. See FACTCHECK.md.

beats.role_note: series continuity — episode 8 built the checker; this week the headline number turns out to be mostly noise
beats.narration_text: Two episodes ago I built the thing that counts contract mismatches between a recipe and its scripts. It reported seven hundred and twenty-five findings, and five hundred and fifty-four of them were one message: this step has no script. But those were recipes marked draft — unbuilt work, honestly described. A draft recipe whose scripts do not exist is not broken. It is a draft.

shot.show: 725 findings, with 554 of them separated out as not-defects
shot.visual_intent: One large stat card reading 725 at the top. Beneath, it divides into two bordered cards: 554 in soft ink labelled 'unbuilt work, correctly described', and 171 in terracotta labelled 'contradicts something the recipe claims'. A short connector runs from the top card to both.

beats.role_note: PROOF rubric — three questions for any count of problems, AS A STRUCTURE before the evidence
beats.narration_text: Three questions for any count of problems. One: does this finding contradict a claim — because if nothing was claimed, nothing can be wrong. Two: which list did you match against — the specific one, or anything that looked similar. Three: did the guard ever fire — because a safety check that never triggers is only evidence if you know it could have.

beats.narration_text: The ask was to stop counting honest states as problems, and then to fix the one that was a real problem.

beats.role_note: QUESTION 1 — the two numbers, reproduced by running the checker read-only
beats.narration_text: Question one, and the answer is a rule rather than a number. A finding is a defect when it contradicts something the recipe claims. Everything else is the honest state of unfinished work, and it gets named rather than counted. That took seven twenty-five to a hundred and seventy-one. Then ninety-one recipes got the status they were missing, and it went to eighty, with ninety recipes now completely clean.
beats.new_visual_element: the two reductions, and the clean count

shot.visual_intent: A horizontal chain of three bordered stat cards: 725, 171, 80, connected by arrows, the last in terracotta. Beneath, a separate bordered card reads 90 clean recipes, with 0 struck beside it — the cross sitting next to the figure, never through it. Citation strip names the command run.

beats.role_note: QUESTION 2 — THE HERO BEAT. The survey that said 42, and what it was matching.
beats.narration_text: Question two, and this is the one that nearly went wrong. Before stamping ninety-one recipes as draft, I checked whether any of them actually had working scripts — because draft would be a lie for those. The first survey came back: forty-two of them do. That would have mislabelled nearly half the batch. But that query matched any path under scripts that a recipe happened to mention, including legacy node scaffolds that exist and do nothing. Narrowed to the six canonical steps in the Script Locations table, the real answer is zero. All ninety-one.

beats.role_note: QUESTION 3 — the guard that never fired, and why that is the point
beats.narration_text: Question three. The generator that writes these refuses to stamp draft on any recipe that does have canonical scripts on disk — it stops instead. Across all ninety-one, that refusal never fired once. Now, a guard that never triggers is usually worth nothing as evidence. It is worth something here for one reason: the forty-two survey proves it could have fired, and would have, if the narrow query had been wrong.
beats.new_visual_element: the guard, and what makes a silent guard meaningful

shot.visual_intent: A bordered panel describing the refusal, with a chip beneath reading 'fired 0 times across 91'. To the right, a terracotta panel giving the condition under which a silent guard is evidence: something has to show it could have fired.

beats.role_note: I made the same error while fact-checking this episode — same shape, same cause
beats.narration_text: And now the part I did not plan. While checking these numbers I ran my own count of how many recipes carry a status line. It came back ninety-eight. The checker says ninety-seven. My command searched the whole recipes folder, so it also matched a YAML file that happens to contain the word status and is not a recipe at all. That is the same mistake as the forty-two, in the same week, committed by the person making a video about it.

beats.role_note: what was verified — the pure prepend, independently, and the todo count that reads two high
beats.narration_text: Verified. The claim is that nothing below line one changed in any of the ninety-one files, and that is checkable from the diff alone: ninety-one files, seven hundred and twenty-eight insertions, zero deletions, and every single hunk starting at line one and adding exactly eight lines. One more detail worth stealing: the open-todo counts are counted per recipe, and markers that appear inside the gate test commands are excluded — because two of the gates grep for todo markers, so a naive count reads two high on every recipe built from the template.
